scr_ap_1099_information_for_the_vendor.purpose: Records on the vendor record which Form 1099 (NEC, MISC, INT) and box the vendor's payments belong to, along with the TIN and 1099 name, so year-end 1099 totals are generated correctly from actual payments.
scr_ap_1099_information_for_the_vendor.outcome: Each reportable vendor carries the right form, box and taxpayer identity, so payments accumulate into accurate year-end 1099 totals automatically.
scr_ap_1099_information_for_the_vendor.rootCause: Property operations pay many unincorporated contractors (make-ready painters, carpet cleaners, handymen, landscapers) plus attorneys for evictions. IRC §6041/§6041A requires 1099 reporting, and the form type depends on the payment nature. Capturing it at vendor setup avoids reconstructing a year of payments in January.
scr_ap_1099_information_for_the_vendor.ifSkipped: Reportable vendors are missed or reported on the wrong form, leading to IRS penalties (IRC §6721/6722), backup withholding exposure, and vendor disputes.
gaap: IRC §3406 — backup withholding when TIN is missing or wrong
redFlags: Vendors paid over $600 with no W-9 or TIN
Attorneys not flagged for 1099 (reportable even when incorporated)
LLCs taxed as corporations flagged as reportable

scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_purch.purpose: Amends an approved purchase order's scope, quantity or price — e.g., additional units added to a flooring contract or an unforeseen repair discovered mid-job — creating a documented, approved change rather than paying invoices that exceed the PO.
scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_purch.outcome: The PO's committed amount reflects the approved revised scope, so invoices can be matched and budget commitments stay accurate.
scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_purch.rootCause: Renovation and repair work routinely changes after approval. Without a change order, invoices exceed the PO, fail matching or bypass approval, and committed costs in the budget are understated. Owners also require approval for scope increases above delegated authority.
scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_purch.ifSkipped: Over-PO invoices get paid without approval, budget commitments are understated, and owners find unapproved overruns during capex reviews.
redFlags: Change orders created after the invoice arrived to force a match
Cumulative change orders exceeding approval limits without escalation
Change orders on capital jobs not reflected in the capex budget

scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_subco.purpose: Records an approved change to a subcontract's value or scope — used in construction and major capital projects where contractors bill against a contract with retainage and schedule of values — so billing and retainage track the revised contract amount.
scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_subco.outcome: Contract value, remaining balance and retainage calculations reflect the approved change, and pay applications can be processed against it.
scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_subco.rootCause: Construction and heavy capex contracts (AIA-style pay applications) change through change orders. Lenders funding draws, owners and auditors expect contract values supported by signed change orders. Without recording them, pay applications exceed contract values and draws cannot be reconciled.
scr_ap_adding_a_change_order_for_a_subco.ifSkipped: Pay applications cannot be reconciled to contract value, retainage is miscalculated, and construction lender draws are delayed or rejected.
redFlags: Change orders without signed documentation
Retainage not recalculated on the revised contract value
Change orders exceeding contingency without owner approval

scr_ap_adding_a_new_purchase_order.purpose: Creates a purchase order before goods or services are ordered — appliances, HVAC replacements, contract services, capital projects — capturing vendor, property, GL coding, amounts and approval routing so the spend is authorized and committed against budget before an invoice exists.
scr_ap_adding_a_new_purchase_order.outcome: An approved commitment that reserves budget, gives the vendor authorization, and provides the reference for matching the invoice later.
scr_ap_adding_a_new_purchase_order.rootCause: Owners delegate spending authority with limits; the only reliable way to enforce them is to require approval before the obligation is created. Purchase orders also give accounting visibility of committed but uninvoiced costs for accruals and budget tracking.
scr_ap_adding_a_new_purchase_order.ifSkipped: Spending happens without authorization, invoices arrive for unapproved work, committed costs are invisible in budget reports, and month-end accruals miss received-but-unbilled goods.
redFlags: POs created after the invoice date (after-the-fact POs)
Splitting purchases into multiple POs to stay under approval limits
Capital items coded to repairs on the PO

scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_credit_or_debit_adj.purpose: Records a vendor credit (credit memo for returned goods, billing error, rebate) or a debit adjustment against a vendor's balance, saved as draft or posted, and applied against open invoices in a later payment.
scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_credit_or_debit_adj.outcome: The vendor balance reflects credits owed to the property, and the credit is used against future payments rather than lost.
scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_credit_or_debit_adj.rootCause: Vendors issue credit memos for returns, overbillings and disputes, and the property may be owed refunds. Unless recorded, the vendor balance and A/P aging overstate what is owed, and credits expire unused.
scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_credit_or_debit_adj.ifSkipped: A/P is overstated, the property overpays vendors, and old unapplied credits linger in the aging with no follow-up.
gaap: ASC 705 — vendor rebates and credits reduce cost
redFlags: Vendor credits older than 90 days unapplied
Credits coded to a different GL than the original invoice
Debit balances in vendor accounts with no refund request

scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_invoice_manually.purpose: Keys a vendor invoice directly into A/P — vendor, invoice number and date, due date, property, GL coding, amounts, PO match and attachments — for invoices not processed through the scanning or Full Service invoice-processing channel.
scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_invoice_manually.outcome: A coded, attached vendor invoice enters the approval workflow and, once approved, becomes a payable (DR expense or asset / CR 2010 Accounts Payable).
scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_invoice_manually.rootCause: Not all invoices arrive through automated capture: urgent repairs, utility shutoff notices, one-off vendors. Manual entry is also where duplicate-invoice and fraudulent-vendor risk is highest, so the screen enforces coding, attachments and routing.
scr_ap_adding_an_a_p_invoice_manually.ifSkipped: Invoices go unrecorded, costs are missed in the period, vendors impose late fees or stop service, and paper invoices get paid outside the system.
gaap: ASC 405 — liability recognition when goods or services are received
COSO 2013 — duplicate payment and invoice authorization controls
redFlags: Same vendor, amount and invoice number entered twice with slight variations
Invoice dated in a prior closed period
Capital projects coded as repairs to avoid capex approval

scr_ap_adding_an_expense_report.purpose: Lets employees (property managers, maintenance supervisors) submit out-of-pocket or corporate-card expenses — supplies bought at a hardware store, mileage, resident event costs — for approval and reimbursement.
scr_ap_adding_an_expense_report.outcome: Approved employee expenses are coded to the right property and GL, and reimbursements are paid through A/P.
scr_ap_adding_an_expense_report.rootCause: Site staff inevitably buy small items outside the PO process. Without a controlled expense report, these costs are reimbursed through petty cash or informal channels, bypassing approval and coding.
scr_ap_adding_an_expense_report.ifSkipped: Reimbursements are paid without approval or receipts, costs hit the wrong property, and personal expenses slip through.
gaap: IRS accountable plan rules (Treas. Reg. §1.62-2) for non-taxable reimbursements
redFlags: Expenses without receipts
Approvers approving their own expense reports
Mileage claims inconsistent with the IRS rate

scr_ap_adding_insurance_or_license_infor.purpose: Records a vendor's certificate of insurance (general liability, workers' compensation, auto) and licenses — carrier, policy number, limits, expiration — so the system can track compliance before vendors work on property.
scr_ap_adding_insurance_or_license_infor.outcome: Vendor compliance data is stored with expiration dates, enabling holds or warnings on vendors with expired coverage.
scr_ap_adding_insurance_or_license_infor.rootCause: Uninsured contractors injured on site or damaging property expose the owner to liability claims. Owners and insurers require vendors to carry minimum coverage with the owner as additional insured. Tracking expiration dates is the only practical way to enforce this across hundreds of vendors.
scr_ap_adding_insurance_or_license_infor.ifSkipped: Uninsured vendors keep working, claims fall on the owner's policy, and insurers may deny coverage or raise premiums.
gaap: Owner insurance requirements / management agreement vendor compliance provisions
redFlags: Expired COIs for active vendors
Coverage limits below owner requirements
Owner not named as additional insured

scr_ap_adding_vendor_supplier_records.purpose: Creates the vendor master record — legal name, remit-to address, TIN, 1099 status, payment terms, payment method and bank details, insurance — that every invoice and payment references.
scr_ap_adding_vendor_supplier_records.outcome: A validated vendor that can receive invoices and payments, with tax and compliance attributes in place.
scr_ap_adding_vendor_supplier_records.rootCause: Vendor master data is the top fraud vector in A/P: fictitious vendors, altered bank details and duplicate vendors used to pay the same invoice twice. Controlled vendor setup with W-9 verification is a foundational control.
scr_ap_adding_vendor_supplier_records.ifSkipped: Duplicate or fictitious vendors appear, 1099 data is incomplete, and payments go to the wrong or fraudulent bank accounts.
redFlags: Duplicate vendors with similar names or the same TIN
Vendors created by the same person who approves their invoices
Vendor addresses matching employee addresses

scr_ap_aging_report.purpose: The curated workflow for the vendor aging and A/P trial balance: unpaid invoices by vendor in 30/60/90/120+ day buckets, reconciled to the 2010 Accounts Payable control account at month-end.
scr_ap_aging_report.outcome: A tied-out A/P subledger and a list of past-due invoices to prioritize for payment or dispute resolution.
scr_ap_aging_report.rootCause: Vendors stop service and add late fees when past due; aging identifies them. The aging total must also equal the GL A/P balance, which is a key balance-sheet reconciliation.
scr_ap_aging_report.ifSkipped: Past-due vendors go unpaid, service is disrupted, and A/P subledger differences go undetected.
redFlags: Aging total not equal to GL 2010
Invoices over 90 days with no dispute note
Debit balances (vendor credits) in the aging

scr_ap_ai_invoice_queue.purpose: Lists invoices that RealPage's AI-Invoice feature has read and pre-coded from scanned or emailed documents — vendor, invoice number, amounts, suggested property and GL — for a human to verify and submit into the approval workflow.
scr_ap_ai_invoice_queue.outcome: Faster invoice entry with AI-suggested coding, while a person confirms accuracy before the invoice becomes a payable.
scr_ap_ai_invoice_queue.rootCause: High invoice volume across portfolios makes manual keying the A/P bottleneck. AI capture reduces keying, but OCR and coding suggestions can be wrong (mis-read amounts, wrong property), so a review queue is needed before posting.
scr_ap_ai_invoice_queue.ifSkipped: AI-captured invoices sit unprocessed (late payments) or get submitted unchecked with wrong amounts or coding.
gaap: COSO 2013 — review of automated inputs (IT application controls)
redFlags: AI-suggested GL codes accepted without checking against the vendor's usual coding
Invoice numbers misread, defeating duplicate detection
Invoices remaining in the queue past their due date

scr_ap_budget_variance_with_commitments_.purpose: Shows, for each GL line, budget versus actual spend plus open commitments (approved POs and subcontracts not yet invoiced), giving the true remaining budget available.
scr_ap_budget_variance_with_commitments_.outcome: A forward-looking budget position that prevents approving new spend on lines already fully committed.
scr_ap_budget_variance_with_commitments_.rootCause: Actual-only reports understate spending because approved POs have not yet been invoiced. Property managers and asset managers need committed costs to avoid overspending, especially on capex and repair lines.
scr_ap_budget_variance_with_commitments_.ifSkipped: Budgets appear to have room when they are already committed, leading to overspending and unapproved variances.
redFlags: Stale open POs inflating commitments
Commitments on lines with no budget
Capex commitments exceeding approved capital budgets

scr_ap_check_run.purpose: The curated workflow for selecting approved vendor invoices and resident refunds for payment by property and bank account, then generating checks, ACH files or wires in a controlled batch.
scr_ap_check_run.outcome: Approved liabilities are paid on time from the correct bank account within available cash, with positive pay and remittance records.
scr_ap_check_run.rootCause: Payments must respect available cash, owner funding, vendor terms and approval status. A structured check run is where the property pays exactly what was approved, from the right account, with fraud controls (positive pay, dual approval) applied.
scr_ap_check_run.ifSkipped: Vendors are paid late (late fees, service stops), unapproved invoices get paid, or payments overdraw operating cash.
gaap: COSO 2013 — payment authorization and segregation of duties
redFlags: Payment run exceeding available cash
Invoices paid before final approval
Same person selecting and releasing payments

scr_ap_closing_the_a_p_subledger.purpose: Closes A/P summaries (the posting buckets for a period) so no further A/P invoices, adjustments or payments post into that period, before the GL period is closed.
scr_ap_closing_the_a_p_subledger.outcome: A/P activity for the period is final, and the A/P aging at period end agrees with the GL.
scr_ap_closing_the_a_p_subledger.rootCause: A/P keeps receiving invoices after month-end. Without a subledger close, late invoices dated in the prior period change reported A/P and expenses after reporting.
scr_ap_closing_the_a_p_subledger.ifSkipped: Late A/P postings alter closed-period expenses and liabilities, and the A/P aging no longer ties to the reported balance sheet.
redFlags: A/P subledger left open after GL close
Summaries reopened without approval
Late invoices posted to closed periods via override

scr_ap_correcting_a_mistake_on_a_1099_fo.purpose: Creates an IRS correction file for 1099s already filed electronically — wrong amount, wrong TIN or name, wrong form type — using the IRS correction procedures (Type 1 and Type 2 corrections).
scr_ap_correcting_a_mistake_on_a_1099_fo.outcome: Corrected information returns filed with the IRS and vendors, limiting penalties and resolving vendor disputes.
scr_ap_correcting_a_mistake_on_a_1099_fo.rootCause: Errors in filed 1099s generate IRS CP2100 B-notices and penalties, and vendors dispute incorrect income amounts. The IRS requires corrections through a specific file process rather than a new original filing.
scr_ap_correcting_a_mistake_on_a_1099_fo.ifSkipped: Penalties accumulate, backup withholding may be required, and vendors complain or dispute their tax reporting.
redFlags: Corrections filed as a new original file (duplicate reporting)
Root cause of the error (vendor setup) not fixed

scr_ap_creating_a_p_invoice_packages.purpose: Bundles selected invoices and their attachments into a single package — for owner reimbursement, lender draw support, capex review or audit requests.
scr_ap_creating_a_p_invoice_packages.outcome: A consolidated, shareable package of invoice support that can be sent to an owner, lender or auditor.
scr_ap_creating_a_p_invoice_packages.rootCause: Owners, lenders and auditors often need copies of many invoices at once — to approve a draw, reimburse the management company or test expenses. Assembling them individually is slow and error-prone.
scr_ap_creating_a_p_invoice_packages.ifSkipped: Draws and reimbursements are delayed, and audit requests take longer, increasing audit fees.
redFlags: Packages missing proof of payment for reimbursement requests
Invoices included that were already reimbursed in a prior draw

scr_ap_exception_queue.purpose: The curated workflow for invoices returned by the RealPage Invoice Processing (Full Service) team with exceptions — missing PO, unknown vendor, invalid property or GL, missing receipt of goods, duplicate suspicion — that must be resolved by the property or accounting team.
scr_ap_exception_queue.outcome: Blocked invoices are resolved and re-enter the workflow before due dates, preventing late fees and service disruption.
scr_ap_exception_queue.rootCause: Outsourced invoice processing cannot resolve business questions (which property, is this a valid vendor, was the work done). Those invoices come back as exceptions, and if nobody owns the queue they age silently.
scr_ap_exception_queue.ifSkipped: Invoices go unpaid, vendors impose late fees or cut service (utilities, trash), and month-end expense is understated.
redFlags: Exceptions older than 10 days
Utility invoices sitting in exceptions near shutoff dates
Exceptions resolved by creating new vendors without verification

scr_ap_exception_report.purpose: Exports all invoices currently blocked in the exception queue, grouped by property and reason, for management follow-up and escalation.
scr_ap_exception_report.outcome: A management view of stuck invoices that drives accountability with site teams and supports month-end accrual of unprocessed invoices.
scr_ap_exception_report.rootCause: Exception queues are invisible to regional managers unless reported. A periodic report lets management chase property managers and quantify unrecorded liabilities at month-end.
scr_ap_exception_report.ifSkipped: Stuck invoices are not escalated, and unprocessed invoices are missed from month-end accruals.
redFlags: Month-end accruals not considering exception-queue invoices
Recurring exceptions from the same property or vendor

scr_ap_guide_to_vendor_1099s.purpose: Overview of the full 1099 cycle in RealPage — flagging vendors, linking reportable payments, running the verification report, generating forms and filing electronically — as the year-end roadmap for the A/P team.
scr_ap_guide_to_vendor_1099s.outcome: A repeatable year-end 1099 process that produces accurate forms by the January 31 deadline.
scr_ap_guide_to_vendor_1099s.rootCause: 1099 compliance depends on data captured all year. The guide exists because errors early in the year (vendor setup) can only be fixed with significant effort in January.
scr_ap_guide_to_vendor_1099s.ifSkipped: Teams run the 1099 process ad hoc, missing steps like TIN verification, and file late or inaccurate returns.
redFlags: 1099 review started only in late January
No TIN matching performed before filing

scr_ap_invoice_research.purpose: A fast search of A/P invoices across properties and statuses — by vendor, invoice number, amount, date, PO — to answer vendor inquiries, investigate duplicates or trace an invoice through approval and payment.
scr_ap_invoice_research.outcome: Quick answers to 'was this invoice received, approved or paid?' and evidence to prevent duplicate entry.
scr_ap_invoice_research.rootCause: Vendors call about unpaid invoices, site teams ask where invoices are, and auditors select samples. Without a research tool, accountants search multiple screens, and duplicates slip through when nobody checks whether an invoice already exists.
scr_ap_invoice_research.ifSkipped: Duplicate invoices are entered and paid, vendor inquiries go unanswered, and audit samples take longer to pull.
redFlags: Duplicate invoice numbers for the same vendor
Invoices paid twice through different payment methods

scr_ap_manage_invoices.purpose: The curated A/P invoice dashboard: search, view, edit, reclassify and track the workflow status of all vendor invoices, including batch entry of multiple invoices.
scr_ap_manage_invoices.outcome: Invoices move efficiently from entry to approval to payment with correct coding and complete support.
scr_ap_manage_invoices.rootCause: Invoice processing is the largest daily workload for offshore teams. A central dashboard makes status visible and prevents invoices from getting stuck between steps.
scr_ap_manage_invoices.ifSkipped: Invoices stall in workflow, coding errors persist, and late payments rise.
redFlags: Invoices pending approval for more than a week
Frequent reclasses from the same property (training issue)

scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices.purpose: The chapter covering how A/P invoices are paid — selection, check printing, ACH and wire payments, manual payments and partial payments — within the constraints of available cash, owner funding and vendor terms.
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices.outcome: A controlled payment cycle that settles approved liabilities on time from the correct accounts.
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices.rootCause: Payment is the point where cash leaves the owner's control. The process must enforce approval, fund availability and fraud controls, and weekly payment cycles must be coordinated with owner funding requests.
scr_ap_paying_a_p_invoices.ifSkipped: Late payments, overdrafts, unapproved payments and fraud exposure.
redFlags: Payments made without owner funding received
Frequent manual or rush payments outside the cycle

scr_ap_purchase_orders_list.purpose: Lists purchase orders with their status (draft, pending approval, approved, partially received, closed) and actions, including job-cost POs, so users can manage open commitments.
scr_ap_purchase_orders_list.outcome: Visibility into open commitments and the ability to close stale POs that inflate committed costs.
scr_ap_purchase_orders_list.rootCause: POs that are never closed keep budget committed and confuse matching. A list with status helps purchasing and accounting keep commitments accurate.
scr_ap_purchase_orders_list.ifSkipped: Stale POs inflate commitments, blocking legitimate spend and misleading budget reports.
redFlags: POs open more than 90 days with no receipts
Fully invoiced POs not closed

scr_ap_receiving_goods_for_a_purchase_or.purpose: Records receipt of goods or completion of services against a PO — the 'receipt of goods' (ROG) step — so the invoice can be three-way matched (PO, receipt, invoice) before payment.
scr_ap_receiving_goods_for_a_purchase_or.outcome: Evidence that the property actually received what it is paying for, which also supports accruing received-but-not-invoiced items at month-end.
scr_ap_receiving_goods_for_a_purchase_or.rootCause: Paying invoices without confirming receipt is a classic fraud and error risk. Three-way matching is the standard control, and receipts also trigger liability recognition when the invoice has not arrived.
scr_ap_receiving_goods_for_a_purchase_or.ifSkipped: The property pays for goods never delivered, and received-not-invoiced liabilities are missed at month-end.
redFlags: Receipts entered after the invoice arrived just to force a match
Receipts entered by the same person who approved the PO

scr_ap_reclassifying_one_invoice.purpose: Changes the coding of a posted A/P invoice — property, GL account, department, job — without changing its amount or payment date, generating correcting GL entries.
scr_ap_reclassifying_one_invoice.outcome: Mis-coded invoices are corrected in the subledger and GL with an audit trail, fixing variance reports without reversing and re-entering the invoice.
scr_ap_reclassifying_one_invoice.rootCause: Invoices are often coded wrong (repairs vs capex, wrong property on shared vendors). Owners require correct coding for NOI and capex reporting, and reversing and re-entering paid invoices would break the payment history.
scr_ap_reclassifying_one_invoice.ifSkipped: Mis-coding stays in the financials, variance explanations become 'coding error' month after month, and capex vs opex is misstated.
redFlags: Reclasses into closed periods
Frequent reclasses between opex and capex near budget deadlines
Reclasses without a note explaining why

scr_ap_recording_a_payment_with_record_t.purpose: Records a payment made by bank transfer (wire or online banking) outside the check run, creating the payment record — and, where approvals are enabled, a payment request that must be approved before it is finalized.
scr_ap_recording_a_payment_with_record_t.outcome: Payments made directly from the bank are reflected in A/P and cash so vendor balances and bank recs stay accurate.
scr_ap_recording_a_payment_with_record_t.rootCause: Some payments (tax bills, insurance, urgent vendor wires) are made directly through bank portals. If not recorded, vendor balances stay open and the bank rec shows unexplained withdrawals.
scr_ap_recording_a_payment_with_record_t.ifSkipped: Vendors appear unpaid and may be paid twice, and bank recs carry unexplained debits.
redFlags: Wires recorded without prior approval
Wire payments to bank accounts different from the vendor master

scr_ap_recording_concessions.purpose: Records a concession — a credit given to a customer or resident as an incentive (waived fees, free rent) — within the payments area, reducing the amount owed.
scr_ap_recording_concessions.outcome: Concessions are reflected as reductions of revenue rather than hidden in expenses or write-offs.
scr_ap_recording_concessions.rootCause: Concessions are common in lease-up and competitive markets. They must be recorded as a revenue reduction (and, under ASC 842, generally straight-lined for leases) so revenue and resident balances are accurate.
scr_ap_recording_concessions.ifSkipped: Concessions are applied as write-offs or not at all, overstating revenue and receivables.
gaap: ASC 842-30 — lease incentives reduce lease income over the lease term
redFlags: Concessions not approved per concession policy
Concessions recorded as bad debt

scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices_list.purpose: Manages recurring vendor invoices — monthly contracts such as elevator maintenance, pest control, laundry leases, cable or software subscriptions — that generate automatically each period.
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices_list.outcome: Fixed recurring costs are recorded every period without manual entry, with a list to monitor and stop them.
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices_list.rootCause: Many vendor contracts bill the same amount monthly, and some never send invoices. Automating them ensures expense is recorded consistently, but they must be monitored when contracts change or end.
scr_ap_recurring_a_p_invoices_list.ifSkipped: Recurring costs are missed or recorded inconsistently, or continue after contracts are cancelled.
redFlags: Recurring invoices for terminated contracts
Amounts not updated after contract escalations
Recurring invoice and an actual vendor invoice both posted for the same month

scr_ap_reversing_an_unpaid_a_p_invoice.purpose: Reverses an unpaid A/P invoice — duplicate, wrong vendor, invoice cancelled by the vendor — creating an offsetting entry instead of deleting it, provided the reversal setting is enabled.
scr_ap_reversing_an_unpaid_a_p_invoice.outcome: The liability and expense are removed with an audit trail, and the invoice cannot be paid.
scr_ap_reversing_an_unpaid_a_p_invoice.rootCause: Posted invoices cannot simply be deleted without destroying the audit trail. Reversal keeps a record of what happened and why, which auditors and owners expect.
scr_ap_reversing_an_unpaid_a_p_invoice.ifSkipped: Invalid invoices remain payable (risk of duplicate payment) and expenses stay overstated.
redFlags: Reversal dated in a closed period
Reversals without documentation from the vendor

scr_ap_running_the_vendor_aging_report_t.purpose: Runs the vendor aging as of period end with settings that match the GL (same as-of date, book and properties) so the total can be reconciled to the 2010 Accounts Payable balance.
scr_ap_running_the_vendor_aging_report_t.outcome: A documented A/P subledger-to-GL reconciliation for the month-end package.
scr_ap_running_the_vendor_aging_report_t.rootCause: A/P and GL can diverge because of manual JEs to the control account, timing of postings or subledger summaries left open. Auditors test this reconciliation because unrecorded or misstated liabilities are a key risk.
scr_ap_running_the_vendor_aging_report_t.ifSkipped: Differences between A/P and GL go undetected and accumulate, eventually requiring unexplained write-offs.
redFlags: Aging run on a different as-of date than the GL
Differences explained as 'timing' without detail

scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_for_electronic.purpose: Enables ACH/electronic payment on a vendor record and captures its bank routing and account details so the vendor can be paid through electronic payment files instead of checks.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_for_electronic.outcome: Vendors are paid faster and more cheaply, with fewer lost or stale checks, once bank details are verified.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_for_electronic.rootCause: Electronic payments reduce check fraud and mailing delays, but changing vendor bank details is the primary business email compromise (BEC) fraud vector. Setup must include independent verification (call-back to a known number).
scr_ap_setting_up_vendors_for_electronic.ifSkipped: The property keeps paying by check (higher cost, check fraud risk), or bank details are set up without verification, exposing it to BEC fraud.
gaap: NACHA Operating Rules — account validation for WEB/CCD entries
redFlags: Bank changes requested by email without call-back verification
Bank details changed shortly before a large payment

scr_ap_vendor_insurance_report.purpose: Lists vendors with their insurance coverage details — insurance type, carrier, policy number, expiration — to identify vendors with expired or missing coverage.
scr_ap_vendor_insurance_report.outcome: A compliance report used to put non-compliant vendors on hold or request updated certificates.
scr_ap_vendor_insurance_report.rootCause: Vendor insurance lapses frequently. Periodic reporting is the practical way to catch expirations before a vendor works on site uninsured.
scr_ap_vendor_insurance_report.ifSkipped: Uninsured vendors continue working, and liability claims fall on the owner.
redFlags: Active vendors with expired coverage
No follow-up on expired certificates

scr_ap_vendor_supplier_aging_report.purpose: Shows amounts owed to each vendor and how long they have been outstanding, optionally as a chart, to manage payment priorities and monitor vendor relationships.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_aging_report.outcome: Visibility of what the property owes, to whom and for how long.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_aging_report.rootCause: Property managers and accounting need to know which vendors are past due to avoid service interruptions and late fees, and to plan cash needs.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_aging_report.ifSkipped: Past-due vendors are overlooked and cash planning is inaccurate.
redFlags: Large balances over 60 days
Unapplied vendor credits

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_insurance_licen.purpose: The vendor record tab holding up to three insurance policies and license details, used to evaluate compliance and drive expiration alerts.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_insurance_licen.outcome: Current coverage and license details are available on the vendor record for compliance checks.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_insurance_licen.rootCause: Compliance requires the data on the vendor record so it can be reported and enforced in approval and payment workflows.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_insurance_licen.ifSkipped: Compliance checks cannot be automated, and vendors work on site without verified coverage.
redFlags: Missing workers' compensation coverage
Licenses expired

scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench.purpose: Shows requesters and approvers the approval status of transactions — invoices, POs, payments, journal entries — including which approver currently holds each item.
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench.outcome: Transparency into approval bottlenecks so items can be escalated before due dates or month-end.
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench.rootCause: Multi-level approval chains (property manager, regional manager, accounting, owner) slow processing. A workbench shows where each item is stuck so it can be followed up.
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench.ifSkipped: Invoices sit with approvers past due dates, and month-end expenses are incomplete.
redFlags: Items pending with an approver who has left the company
Approvals bypassed via delegation to the requester

scr_ap_void_reissue.purpose: The curated workflow for voiding lost, expired, returned or erroneous vendor checks and either reissuing payment or restoring the invoice to open status.
scr_ap_void_reissue.outcome: Voided checks are removed from outstanding items and the vendor is paid correctly, with positive pay updated.
scr_ap_void_reissue.rootCause: Checks get lost in the mail, go stale or are issued in error. Voiding correctly keeps the bank rec and vendor balance accurate and prevents both the original and replacement from clearing.
scr_ap_void_reissue.ifSkipped: Stale checks inflate outstanding items, vendors remain unpaid, or both the original and replacement checks clear.
redFlags: Voids without stop payment or positive pay update
Stale checks voided instead of escheated

scr_ap_voiding_a_check.purpose: Voids a printed check — misprint, wrong amount, payment deferred — discarding the check number and making the invoice available for payment again, with the void recorded in the chosen period.
scr_ap_voiding_a_check.outcome: The check is removed from cash disbursements and the invoice returns to open status.
scr_ap_voiding_a_check.rootCause: Printing errors and changed payment decisions are routine. Voiding with an audit trail keeps check sequence control intact and prevents voided checks from being cashed.
scr_ap_voiding_a_check.ifSkipped: Printed but unusable checks remain outstanding, sequences have gaps without explanation, and the invoice cannot be repaid.
